The best next experiment is **uniform multi-negative softmax training**, keeping SASRec unchanged. At 0% research progress, this isolates a training-objective hypothesis before adding architectural complexity.

**Insights from the starting point.** Electronics has the weakest observed training separation: 13.08% of sampled negatives outrank positives. This motivates testing discrimination, but does not establish a validation deficit. The recent-residual inspiration already tests explicit local similarity. Changing the objective provides a complementary experiment without adding another history branch. Qualitative feedback identifies unsupported practical associations. Histories and text cannot establish ownership or satisfied needs, so these judgments should remain exploratory audits rather than negative labels.

**Insights from related work.** Sampling-reliability research [1] distinguishes sampled evaluation from full-catalog ranking. Keep host HR@10 as the selection criterion and qualify broader claims. The sequential negative-sampling study [2] reports frequency-dependent tradeoffs. Start with uniform competitors and inspect training-frequency strata before introducing popularity bias. BSARec [3] motivates investigating representation smoothing. Existing cosine alignment values do not establish that mechanism, so architectural remedies require stronger evidence.

**Framework and directions.**

| Direction | Intervention | Evidence needed |
|---|---|---|
| Ranking discrimination | Multiple uniform competitors | Host macro HR@10; sampled margins |
| History specificity | Existing recent residual | Backbone/residual controls |
| Evidence sufficiency | Supported/conflict/unknown audit | Explicit history or text evidence |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of ten; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each cell gives a positive and a limitation.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|
| Eight-negative softmax [1,2] | 2: distinct next experiment; established objective | 7: tests discrimination; unlabeled negatives may be relevant | 3: small loss change; sampling needs care |
| Last-item versus five-item residual | 3: isolates window benefit; substantial precedent | 6: tests local context; may favor redundancy | 3: small branch; predictor parity required |
| TF-IDF competitor mixture [2] | 4: tests textual specificity; familiar mining | 6: challenges broad matches; false negatives likely | 5: no pretrained weights; indexing adds cost |

**Selected algorithm.** At every valid causal position, score the observed next item against eight unique uniformly sampled training-catalog items, preserving baseline history exclusions. Minimize cross-entropy over these nine logits. This supplies multiple competing gradients; improvement remains a hypothesis. Keep tied embeddings, architecture, optimizer and training schedule fixed.

```text
for sequence, positive in training_batches:
    features = SASRec(sequence)
    negatives = uniform_unique_items(K=8, baseline_exclusions)
    logits = score(features, concat(positive, negatives))
    loss = cross_entropy(logits[valid_positions], target_column=0)
    update(loss)
```

Compare baseline BCE, one-negative softmax and eight-negative softmax within the shared budget. Preserve all four routes, required seeds, splits, environment paths and default 200 epochs. Keep inference scoring unchanged and verify generated predictor parity. Preserve DiagnosisProbe, restore model mode, and distinguish loader-negative diagnostics from training competitors. Select solely by host macro validation HR@10; report no inferred test gains.

References: [1](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086), [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276), [3](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28747).

idea.description: Replace the baseline training loss with cross-entropy over one observed positive and eight unique uniform negative items per valid causal position, retaining the baseline SASRec architecture and inference scores.
idea.motivation: Electronics shows the weakest supplied training margins, while qualitative feedback suggests broad associations can outrank specific matches. Multiple competitors provide a minimal test of ranking discrimination without assuming that missing ownership, compatibility or intent evidence constitutes dislike. Neither diagnosis establishes that this change will improve validation HR@10.
idea.implementation_notes: Use DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']. Preserve Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl, original dataset routing and splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and SASREC_EPOCHS with default 200. Write artifacts beneath the trial directory and use one GPU per trial. Preserve baseline architecture, initialization, optimizer and checkpoint rules. Sample negatives using training-catalog IDs and the baseline training-history exclusions; exclude padding, the positive and duplicate competitors. Do not consult validation or test histories to construct exclusions. If fewer than eight eligible items exist, use all eligible items and mask missing competitor slots. Apply cross-entropy to raw tied-embedding logits with temperature 1 and average over valid positions. Uniform sampling needs no relative probability correction among eligible negatives; this objective is not an unbiased full-catalog softmax estimator. Compare baseline BCE, one-negative softmax and eight-negative softmax to distinguish objective changes from competitor-count changes. Log all compute against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Inference remains the trained dot-product scorer; retain the predictor writer and verify saved/reloaded score parity across all four routes. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions; view.model remains the trained module. Restore its prior training mode in finally. Preserve existing loader-negative diagnostics and label optional multi-competitor diagnostics separately. Keep unavailable metadata breakdowns empty and return null for undefined statistics. Select using the unchanged host macro validation HR@10 only. Full-catalog recommendations for the twenty training users remain exploratory qualitative evidence.
idea.pseudocode:
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

def multi_negative_loss(features, positive, negatives, item_emb):
    # features: [B,L,D]; positive: [B,L]; negatives: [B,L,K]
    # Sampling must enforce baseline exclusions and uniqueness upstream.
    valid = positive.ne(0)
    if not valid.any():
        return features.sum() * 0.0
    candidates = torch.cat([positive.unsqueeze(-1), negatives], dim=-1)
    logits = torch.einsum('bld,blkd->blk', features, item_emb(candidates))
    # Zero negative IDs represent absent competitors in small catalogs.
    allowed = candidates.ne(0)
    logits = logits.masked_fill(~allowed, float('-inf'))
    logits = logits[valid]
    labels = torch.zeros(logits.shape[0], dtype=torch.long, device=logits.device)
    return F.cross_entropy(logits, labels)

# Train unchanged SASRec with K=8 unique uniform eligible negatives.
# Compare with baseline BCE and K=1 softmax under matched settings.
# Save category checkpoints and generate the matching baseline predictor.
# Verify scoring/reload/routing parity; select using host macro validation HR@10.

originality.positive: Provides an objective-level experiment distinct from the previous recent-history residual.
originality.negative: Multi-negative softmax is established; this is a controlled application rather than a new algorithmic principle.

future_potential.positive: Offers a simple foundation for testing whether competitor count and sampling distribution explain category-specific ranking weaknesses.
future_potential.negative: Unobserved items can be relevant, and improvements under sampled validation may not transfer to full-catalog recommendation.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires a sampler and loss change while preserving architecture, checkpoint format and inference scoring.
code_difficulty.negative: Unique eligible sampling, small-catalog handling and fair objective controls require care and additional training budget.

related_work.title: Sampling reliability study, RecSys 2025
contributions: The supplied summary distinguishes sampled-metric resolution, fidelity, robustness and recovery of model rankings.
limitations: Does not establish that increasing training negatives improves this pinned benchmark.
Sampled validation gains do not establish full-catalog gains.

related_work.title: Sequential recommendation negative-sampling study, 2024
contributions: The supplied summary reports different head, middle and tail behavior across negative-sampling methods.
limitations: Aggregate tradeoffs depend on datasets and evaluation settings.
Popularity-based or harder negatives can include relevant unobserved items.

contributions: Investigates attention oversmoothing and introduces frequency-based sequential modeling.
limitations: The supplied embedding alignment statistics do not establish oversmoothing in the current model.
